# dsh-plugin-subagent-delete
DeepSeek Harness (DSH) plugin that adds the missing subagent lifecycle interface:

- `delete_subagent` — permanently delete a subagent session and drop it from the session list
- `rel

ease_subagent` — stop / release a subagent without deleting its transcript
- `list_subagents` — list
the calling session's descendant subagents (including finished one-shot subagents)

Verified against DSH `0.2.1-alpha.2`; compatibility shims keep `0.2.0-rc.2` and
`>=0.1.0-rc.8 <0.2.0
## Why

DSH's built-in subagent control surface only provides `send_message`, `interrupt_agent`
and `list_ag

ents`. There is no delete/release endpoint, so finished one-shot and stale
continuable subagents kee

p accumulating in the web UI list. This plugin fills that gap
with an ownership-checked, model-calla
ble tool plus optional HTTP routes.

not be read carries `unreadable`

Without `recursive: true` a target that still has descendants is refused with

## Web UI auto-refresh

A permanent delete removes the durable child, but an open client keeps its
cached session list and p

rojections until something invalidates them. This
plugin works around that gap without patching DSH:

after every permanent delete
the host publishes a short-lived marker session through the official
`

prepare → enter → announce → detach` lifecycle seam. The bundled web client
component (`lib/client.j

s`) watches the public `sessions.list` snapshot and,
when the marker child is removed (`api-session/

removed`), debounces 350 ms and
calls `sessions.refresh()` plus `sessions.refreshProjections(parentI

d)` for the
affected parents — the current dsh face (pre-0.2.1 releases used
`sessions.refreshSubage

nts(parentId)` and are still supported). Open web clients
therefore drop the deleted subagent withou

t a manual page reload. The marker's
`_no-cwd` artifact is swept after detach, so the refresh glue l

eload. The marker's
`_no-cwd` artifact is swept after detach, so the refresh glue leaves no residue.

Team sessions additionally lose the teammate from the Team panel: a teammate is
a durable `team/memb

er` fact, and `delete_subagent` terminates it through the
official Lead-only dismissal before removi

delete_subagent` terminates it through the
official Lead-only dismissal before removing the Session.

One honest limit remains: the parent Session's `subagent/catalog` facts are
append-only durable hist

ory, so a deleted child can still appear as a
**historical row** in the parent's header catalog drop

down until that parent log
itself moves on. Removing the fact would mean rewriting a committed sessi

on
log, which dsh does not support. The sidebar session list is refreshed
normally.
## HTTP routes (web profiles)
For client integration and local debugging the host plugin registers:

- `GET  /dsh-plugin-subagent-delete/list?parentSessionId=<id>[&activity=…][&mode=…]`
- `POST /dsh-pl
ugin-subagent-delete/delete` `{ "parentSessionId": "<id>", "subagentId": "<id>", "recursive": false

}`
- `POST /dsh-plugin-subagent-delete/release` `{ "parentSessionId": "<id>", "subagentId": "<id>",
"recursive": false }`

HTTP callers must name the same `parentSessionId` the target descends from; the
same ownership check
runs on every mutation.
## Safety

- A subagent can only be deleted by its own session-tree ancestor. Foreign or
unknown ids return `no

t-your-subagent`; an id whose durable session is already
gone returns `already_absent` rather than a

hard failure.
- Running subagents are cancelled and awaited (15s quiescence bound) before
their fil

es are removed; the timeout never leaves a pending timer behind.
- File removal is confirmed before

workspace accounting is stripped, so a
failed delete cannot produce a half-removed row.
